```plato

    // Unwelded triangle soup turned into an indexed mesh with shared vertices:
    // `ToTriangleMesh` supplies the identity index table and this merges it down.
    // This is the pass marching-cubes output (`voxels.library.plato`) needs before
    // anything topological can be asked of it.
    Welded(self: TriangleArray3D, tolerance: Number): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.ToTriangleMesh.Welded(tolerance);

    //==
    // # Edge split
    //
    // Refinement. A per-edge decision array says which edges gain a midpoint; each
    // triangle then re-triangulates according to how many of its three edges were
    // chosen — the red-green refinement cases, 1-to-2, 1-to-3 and 1-to-4
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_refinement).
    //
    // The new vertices are APPENDED to the position array in edge order, so old
    // vertex numbers survive the pass unchanged. That is what lets Loop and
    // Butterfly subdivision below reuse this function for their topology and
    // simply supply a different position array of the same shape.

    // The vertex number of the midpoint introduced on each undirected edge, or -1
    // where the edge is not split. New vertices are numbered by the edge's rank
    // among the split edges, after the existing vertices.
    SplitVertexNumbers(splitMask: Array<Boolean>, baseVertexCount: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => splitMask.Count.MapRange(e => VertexIndex(splitMask[e]
            ? baseVertexCount + e.MapRange(d => splitMask[d] ? 1 : 0).Reduce(0, (acc, hit) => acc + hit)
            : -1));

    // The midpoints introduced by a split, in edge order: the block appended to
    // the position array.
    SplitMidpoints(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, splitMask: Array<Boolean>): Array<Point3D>
        => splitMask.Count.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(Repeat(0, Point3D.Origin), (acc, e) =>
            splitMask[e] ? acc.Append(self.EdgeMidpoint(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e))) : acc);

    // How one triangle re-triangulates when some of its edges carry a new midpoint.
    // v0, v1, v2 are the corners in winding order; m0 sits on v0-v1, m1 on v1-v2
    // and m2 on v2-v0, each the "none" index when that edge was not split. Every
    // emitted triangle keeps the original winding.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.
    SplitFaceTriangles(v0: VertexIndex, v1: VertexIndex, v2: VertexIndex,
                       m0: VertexIndex, m1: VertexIndex, m2: VertexIndex): Array<TriangleFace>
    {
        var s0 = m0.IsPresent;
        var s1 = m1.IsPresent;
        var s2 = m2.IsPresent;
        return s0.And(s1).And(s2)
            ? [TriangleFace(v0, m0, m2), TriangleFace(m0, v1, m1),
               TriangleFace(m2, m1, v2), TriangleFace(m0, m1, m2)]
            : (s0.And(s1)
            ? [TriangleFace(m0, v1, m1), TriangleFace(v0, m0, m1), TriangleFace(v0, m1, v2)]
            : (s1.And(s2)
            ? [TriangleFace(m1, v2, m2), TriangleFace(v0, v1, m1), TriangleFace(v0, m1, m2)]
            : (s0.And(s2)
            ? [TriangleFace(v0, m0, m2), TriangleFace(m0, v1, v2), TriangleFace(m0, v2, m2)]
            : (s0 ? [TriangleFace(v0, m0, v2), TriangleFace(m0, v1, v2)]
            : (s1 ? [TriangleFace(v0, v1, m1), TriangleFace(v0, m1, v2)]
            : (s2 ? [TriangleFace(v0, v1, m2), TriangleFace(m2, v1, v2)]
            : [TriangleFace(v0, v1, v2)]))))));
    }

    // Every masked edge split at once. Old vertices keep their numbers and the
    // midpoints follow them in edge order.
    SplitEdges(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, splitMask: Array<Boolean>): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var midpointOf = SplitVertexNumbers(splitMask, self.Positions.Count);
        return (self.Positions.Concatenate(self.SplitMidpoints(topology, splitMask)),
                self.Faces.Count.MapRange(f => f).FlatMap(f =>
                    SplitFaceTriangles(
                        self.Faces[f].A, self.Faces[f].B, self.Faces[f].C,
                        midpointOf[topology.CornerEdges[f * 3].Value],
                        midpointOf[topology.CornerEdges[f * 3 + 1].Value],
                        midpointOf[topology.CornerEdges[f * 3 + 2].Value])));
    }

    // One undirected edge split at its midpoint: each incident triangle becomes
    // two. The single-operator form of `SplitEdges`.
    SplitEdge(self: TriangleMesh3D, edge: UndirectedEdgeIndex): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return self.SplitEdges(topology, SingleEdgeMask(topology.EdgeCount, edge));
    }

    // Every edge longer than `maxLength` split once. One pass halves a long edge,
    // so an edge several times the target needs several passes — which is what the
    // iteration count of `IsotropicRemeshed` below supplies.
    SplitLongEdges(self: TriangleMesh3D, maxLength: Number): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return self.SplitEdges(topology, topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e =>
            self.EdgeLength(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)) > maxLength));
    }

    //==
    // # Edge collapse
    //
    // Coarsening. In a mutable remesher a collapse invalidates the indices of
    // everything around it, so collapses are done one at a time against a
    // structure that is repaired after each one. Here every candidate is judged
    // against the same mesh and the accepted ones are applied together, which
    // needs a conflict rule instead: no two accepted collapses may have ADJACENT
    // endpoints, and edges are considered in edge order. A candidate rejected this
    // pass is simply reconsidered in the next one.
    //
    // Merely forbidding a SHARED endpoint is not enough, and this is the subtle
    // part. Take two collapses whose endpoints are neighbours of one another, and
    // a triangle holding one endpoint of each plus some third vertex: after both
    // collapses that triangle, and another one just like it, become the SAME
    // triangle, and the mesh has a doubled face where it had two distinct ones.
    // Requiring the whole one-ring of each endpoint to be free rules that out, at
    // the cost of accepting fewer collapses per pass.
    //
    // On top of that, every candidate must satisfy the LINK CONDITION, which is
    // what stops a collapse from pinching the surface. It is enforced inside
    // `CollapseEdges` rather than left to callers, because it is a property of
    // contraction itself and not a policy: an edge that fails it has no correct
    // collapse. A single-edge `CollapseEdge` on such an edge therefore returns the
    // mesh unchanged.
    //
    // What is still NOT checked is fold-over: a collapse that keeps the mesh a
    // manifold can still invert a nearby triangle when the surviving position is
    // far from both endpoints. The quadric minimizer is the usual source, and a
    // caller that cares can decimate in more, smaller passes.

    // True when a vertex appears in a neighbour row.
    RowContains(row: Array<VertexIndex>, vertex: VertexIndex): Boolean
        => row.Any(n => n.Value == vertex.Value);

    // How many vertices neighbour BOTH ends of an edge.
    SharedNeighborCount(neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>, pair: VertexPair): Integer
        => neighbors[pair.A.Value]
            .Map(n => RowContains(neighbors[pair.B.Value], n) ? 1 : 0)
            .Reduce(0, (acc, hit) => acc + hit);

    // The link condition (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge_contraction): an edge
    // may be contracted without changing the surface's topology exactly when the
    // vertices adjacent to BOTH its endpoints are precisely the apexes of the
    // triangles sharing it — two in the interior, one on a boundary. Two joined
    // vertices with a third common neighbour elsewhere form a tunnel one edge
    // wide, and contracting that pinches the surface shut.
    //
    // Cheap, despite appearances: with a neighbour table already built, the test
    // is the product of two valences, so it costs about the same as reading the
    // edge.
    SatisfiesLinkCondition(topology: TriangleMeshTopology, neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>, e: Integer): Boolean
        => SharedNeighborCount(neighbors, topology.UndirectedEdges[e])
            == (topology.IsBoundaryEdge(UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)) ? 1 : 2);

    // True when a vertex and every one of its neighbours is still free.
    HasFreeNeighborhood(state: Array<Integer>, neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>, vertex: Integer): Boolean
        => (state[vertex] == -1).And(neighbors[vertex].All(n => state[n.Value] == -1));
```
